title: Windowed stream consolidation and KV slab balance for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Mixed-length traffic (short prompts with long responses and vice versa) causes KV cache fragmentation and GPU slab imbalance. Continuous (streaming) request admission currently leads to many small slots and uneven KV residency, increasing per-token cost and causing transient OOMs under load spikes. Goal: introduce a windowed stream consolidation layer + KV slab balancer to reduce fragmentation, control KV residency hotspots, and improve p95 latency at steady throughput without regressions in mean latency or quality.

Scope: scheduler admission logic, slot/window coalescing heuristics, KV slab residency tracking, GPU slab balancing policy, eviction watermark tuning, metrics & dashboards, unit/integration tests, and canary rollout plan. Not in scope: model architecture changes, end-user API surface changes, or permanent changes to customer-facing config names (we'll use gate flags).
acceptance_criteria: P95 inference latency for mixed prompt/response profile improves by >= 12% over baseline at target throughput (1000 req/s on p3dn-like profile)
KV cache fragmentation (measured as number of distinct small segments per slab) decreases by >= 30% under the same workload
No increase in token-level quality regressions as measured by evaluation harness (prompt set A) beyond 0.5%
OOM events on GPU clusters do not increase; target is zero new OOMs during a 24-hour stress run
Feature guarded with runtime flag; rollout plan includes staged canary with automatic rollback on latency or error regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests for window coalescer and admission policy (edge cases: extremely skewed length distributions)
Integration tests that simulate mixed-length workload with synthetic arrival traces (preserve token interleaving semantics)
Stress test in staging with same hardware profile as production (p3dn / a100 equivalent) for 24 hours
A/B canary in production with 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% gates, monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, kv-residency, and token throughput
Compare outputs against golden set to ensure no quality regressions
metrics_and_dashboards: latency.p50, latency.p95, latency.p99 per-model and per-route
implementation_notes: Introduce a sliding 'consolidation window' (default 30ms, configurable) that groups incoming streaming slots when safe (same model & compatible temperature/params). This reduces small-slot churn and allows contiguous KV allocations.

Add a KV Slab Balancer that periodically (every N allocations) computes a lightweight rebalancing plan: prefer filling underutilized slabs with longer-residency sequences and steer admission to balance residency ratios across GPUs.

Admission policy will consider three signals: incoming sequence length estimate, per-route priority, and current slab hotness (hotness = average KV reads+writes per-slot over last 500ms). Reject/admit with backpressure hints rather than outright drops.
Eviction watermark tuning: raise soft eviction watermark by 5% during stabilization window to avoid premature compaction churn; hard eviction unchanged.
Keep strong invariants: correctness of KV pointers, no cross-slab aliasing, and strict per-request isolation for privacy/compliance.
Expose runtime flags: enable_windowed_consolidation, consolidation_window_ms, kv_slab_balancer_enabled, slab_balancer_interval_ms
Start with conservative defaults (window 30ms, balancer interval 2000ms) and ramp via feature flag in canary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-consolidation could add tail latency for latency-sensitive short requests. Mitigation: per-route latency SLO guardrail (bypass consolidation if route p95 > threshold) and upper bound on per-request enqueue delay (max 50ms).

Risk: Balancer logic could thrash allocations and increase eviction churn. Mitigation: balancer produces soft steering hints and uses hysteresis; requires two consecutive triggers before force-migration actions.
Risk: Unexpected correctness bugs in KV pointer management. Mitigation: thorough unit tests, integration tests with pointer-checker, and short canary windows with memory-snapshot diffing.
Risk: Increased CPU overhead for balancer bookkeeping. Mitigation: keep metrics sketch-based (approx counters) and throttle balancer frequency.
Operational risk: rollout could interact with autoscaling heuristics. Mitigation: coordinate with infra team and schedule canary during low-impact window; include autoscaling metrics in alerting.
Security/Compliance: ensure balancer does not leak tenant identifiers in logs; scrub any slab identifiers in telemetry where applicable.
